summary: ArmoniSat (Argentina Fire Calendar) is a static web app that puts every week of NASA FIRMS daytime hot spots, from November 2000 to November 2026, on one scale for Argentina and its 24 provinces: VIIRS 375 m, afternoon orbit. MODIS years are converted with a factor k, the ratio of Suomi NPP VIIRS to Aqua MODIS hot spots in 2013–2022, per province and season. In San Luis the raw record shows daytime hot spots rising from 1,028 a year (Aqua MODIS, 2003–2011) to 2,474 (Suomi NPP VIIRS, 2013–2022), an apparent 2.4-fold increase. On one scale they go from 4,078 to 2,446, down 40 %, and Aqua alone shows the same drop. These are detections: we do not claim that fire decreased. Errors are measured on held-out years of 2013–2022; before 2012 no VIIRS data exist, so the error there cannot be measured.
details:
Is a week of fire in San Luis high, normal or low? Answering needs every week of NASA FIRMS hot spots from 2000 to 2026 on one scale.

WHAT IT DOES

Choose Argentina or one of its 24 provinces, from the map, from the list or by entering a latitude and longitude. A calendar of 27 years by 53 weeks colours each week against the usual for that week or by hot spot count. Any year from 2000 to 2026 reads week by week against the median and the 10th–90th percentile range of the same week, and month by month against the monthly median. The reference period can be 2001–2025 or the VIIRS years only (2012–2025). The data download as CSV for any range of years, and each chart downloads as an SVG file.

The area of interest is a province, because the factor is calibrated per province: free-drawn areas are not supported. The CSV holds weekly totals, not individual detections.

HOW IT WAS VALIDATED

For each year of 2013–2022, k is computed from the other nine years and converted MODIS has to predict what VIIRS measured.

Weekly error per province, daytime, held-out years 2013–2022, all provinces pooled: one national factor 27.1 %, ours 22.7 % (median province 31 %, San Luis 33.1 %). Two VIIRS sensors of the same design, passing at different times, disagree by 18.2 % (2020–2025).

San Luis, daytime, held-out years 2013–2022: average error of 3.7 % on the yearly total, 19.4 % on monthly totals and 33.1 % on weekly totals.

Across all provinces, in held-out daytime weeks of 2013–2022, the converted class matches the VIIRS class 58 % of the time (25 % by chance) and falls within one class 94 % (66 % by chance): read a pre-2012 week as high, normal or low, no finer.

The uncertainty band, nominally 90 %, covers 91.4 % of held-out daytime weeks when its percentiles are estimated without the evaluated year.

Control without conversion: Aqua MODIS flew through both periods. In San Luis, VIIRS-scale detections go from 4,078 a year (2003–2011) to 2,446 (2013–2022), down 40 %, and Aqua alone shows the same drop. The calendar inherits that change; it does not create it.

LIMITS

Errors are measured on held-out years of 2013–2022. Before 2012 no VIIRS data exist, so the error there cannot be measured. 2012, never used for calibration, is predicted with a +1.2 % national bias.

"Usual" (2001–2025) mixes converted and measured years. We cannot tell less fire from a change in detection.

In San Luis the years that rank highest on the converted scale (2003, 2002, 2001, 2009) are all converted MODIS years; 2001 and the first half of 2002 rely on Terra and are low confidence. On held-out years the Terra chain misses weekly totals by 43.7 %, and in the second half of 2002 it falls 11 to 16 % below Aqua.

A hot spot is not a fire and not a burned area: it is a thermal detection in one pixel at the moment the satellite passed. Zero hot spots does not mean no fire. Night detections are left out.

The app is in Spanish, with an English version at https://fibodev.com/armonisat/en/. It is not an alert system.

HOW IT WAS HARMONIZED

Each MODIS week is multiplied by a factor k: the ratio of Suomi NPP VIIRS to Aqua MODIS daytime hot spots in 2013–2022, when both crossed Argentina at the same time of day. There is one factor per province and season; where a province has under 200 Aqua hot spots in a season, the factor of its region or of the country is used instead.

From 2012 the calendar shows measured VIIRS: Suomi NPP, the average of Suomi NPP and NOAA-20 from 2020, and the average of NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 after Suomi NPP ended on 2 November 2026. From November 2000 to mid-2002 only Terra MODIS was flying; it needs two factors and is the weakest stretch. MODIS is not used after 2012.

Detections that NASA labels as static sources are dropped, and so is everything inside small cells with a history of such labels. Only daytime detections are shown.

WHO IT IS FOR

Built for whoever must say if a week is unusual: a provincial fire office, the national fire management service. In San Luis, August to October hold 62 % of typical monthly activity. Built for them, not yet tested with them.

PRODUCT CONCEPT (NOT BUILT YET)

The weekly status of a province fits in one short text message, under 200 bytes. A small script in the project already writes it from the same data the app reads. That makes it possible to relay it over an off-grid LoRa mesh (Meshtastic) to fire crews in areas with no mobile signal, such as the hills of San Luis. Nothing has been sent over a radio or tested in the field.

TOOLS

TypeScript, React, Vite and three.js for the app, which is a static site with no server and loads nothing from third parties at run time. Python (pandas, NumPy, Shapely) for the data processing. Code and text were written with AI assistance and reviewed by the team. Code: https://github.com/marianograziano/armonisat

HOW IT ANSWERS THE CHALLENGE

Hot spots from the early 2000s to today, by region → "Fire calendar for {region}" → FIRMS MODIS × k before 2012; FIRMS VIIRS since 2012.

Periods and years with most activity; this week and this month against the historical median → "{region} week by week" and "{region} month by month" → weekly and monthly medians, 2001–2025.

Sensor of origin made comparable → "Can the years before 2012 be trusted?" → Aqua MODIS and Suomi NPP VIIRS, 2013–2022.

Select a region and a date range, download analytics and visualizations → "Find by coordinates", year range for the CSV, "Download this chart (SVG)" → weekly totals.

TEAM

MajorTom, one member, San Luis local event (Argentina).
